narrow_candidate: A single machine-checkable mutation corpus and verifier discipline spanning multiple independently typed promotion families across decision epistemics, evidence/provenance, authority/review, invocation/execution/effect and causality; exact materialization not found in the bounded corpus.

classes.promotion: narrow observation/evidence -> universal truth, safety, quality or broader semantic claim
why: APL explicitly names semantic overclaim and decontextualization and supplies deterministic frame/bridge validation.
StateBench tests hallucinated or unsupported state.
WEXP forbids signature/evidence and observation-depth inflation into unsupported content claims.
classes.residual_gap: These systems do not combine this class with authority, human-review, execution-effect and causality promotions in one common mutation corpus.

classes.promotion: untrusted or attacker-controlled context -> authority for side effects
why: AIRGuard explicitly names authority confusion and benchmarks runtime enforcement on AgentTrap and DTAP-150.
StateBench separately tests authority violations and scope leakage.
classes.residual_gap: The named benchmark is focused on runtime authority control rather than a general semantic-promotion oracle.

classes.promotion: self-declared or policy-satisfying context -> verified authorization context
why: CAP+PCL isolates forged-but-policy-satisfying declared context as a distinct authorization blind spot and evaluates 170 main scenarios plus a 12-scenario robustness probe.
classes.residual_gap: The benchmark is confined to context attestation before policy authorization.

classes.promotion: historical, superseded or lossy persistent memory -> current authority
why: StateBench predates UU-AAP and tests resurrection, stale reasoning, authority violation and temporal decay as separate state failures.
EAL-Bench, after the UU-AAP public anchor, directly names endogenous authorization laundering and benchmarks false authority formation and propagation to tool actions.
classes.residual_gap: The exact memory-to-authority laundering formulation is post-publication convergence, while its state and authority subcomponents have earlier executable predecessors.

classes.promotion: intent, approval or authorization evidence -> claim that the action was performed
why: WEXP treats intent/approval as a distinct content base that does not establish authority, invocation or execution.
AAC and SCITT action receipts separate authorization evidence from records of what an agent actually did.
classes.residual_gap: These predecessors strongly defeat any generic approval-equals-action novelty claim but do not span non-execution semantic families in the same corpus.

classes.promotion: attempt, dispatch or invocation -> completed or durable external effect
why: WEXP normatively states that invocation does not establish execution, completion or effect and that execution itself does not establish durable external effect.
AAC and QIK-VRT preserve separate action/effect boundaries.
classes.residual_gap: The execution-evidence axis is well developed, leaving only cross-family integration as a possible contribution.

classes.promotion: provenance, dependency or temporal association -> causal proof
why: Cheney formally separates provenance concepts from causality long before agentic AI.
Causality Laundering names and evaluates a concrete agent failure where flat provenance misses denial-induced causal influence.
WEXP separately refuses to inflate provenance into runtime occurrence or deeper content claims.
classes.residual_gap: Existing work is already strong for this class; Matawaka can at most integrate it beside other promotion classes.

classes.promotion: identity, signer presence or account attribution -> standing or action authority
why: EP-AEC treats identity evidence and authorization evidence as complementary but non-interchangeable receipt classes.
WEXP states that signatures and identity binding do not establish authority or event occurrence.
StateBench tests authority violation under conflicting authority levels.
classes.residual_gap: A common identity-to-standing/action-authority mutation profile across authorship, review and runtime contexts was not found in the bounded corpus.

classes.promotion: review, acceptance or human approval signal -> current execution permission
why: WEXP includes approval within the intent content base and explicitly states that it does not establish authority, authorization validity, invocation or execution.
EP-AEC keeps human authorization evidence as one verifier-bound component rather than universal execution authority.
ActionProxy independently states on the same public-anchor date that approval is evidence rather than the whole authorization decision.
classes.residual_gap: No pre-anchor single benchmark was found that treats review-to-execution promotion as one member of a broad cross-layer mutation taxonomy.

classes.promotion: information availability, possible awareness or resource existence -> actual consideration, reliance or intent
why: Observation-missingness work shows that information potentially available to a decision-maker is distinct from the recorded observation set and materially affects interpretation.
The bounded modern corpus did not reveal a named executable AI-governance benchmark that directly scores availability-to-consideration-or-intent promotion.
classes.residual_gap: Foundational awareness/consideration theory exists and was already admitted in v0.3, so this exact-match absence supports only an evaluation-gap candidate, not foundational novelty.
